questions.q: Per the Definition of Done, which chapter is responsible for implementing the role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules?
options: Chapter 4 — Analytics and Delivery
Chapter 1 — Design
Chapter 3 — Build: Automation and Security
Chapter 2 — Build: Data and Objects
questions.explain: The requirements table maps the role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules requirement to Chapter 3, where the security model designed in Chapter 1 gets implemented.

questions.q: Which chapter in this capstone is described as "purely additive," and what does that mean for build order?
options: Chapter 1, because it only contains planning lessons
Chapter 3, because Flows add new fields automatically
Chapter 2, because every lesson in it creates a brand-new object
Chapter 4, because it never changes the object model -- it only uses what already exists
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls Chapter 4 purely additive: its reports, dashboard, and sample data use the object model and automation already built, without changing it.

questions.q: Which standard object holds the specific equipment products attached to one deal at Cascade?
options: Campaign
Opportunity Product (Line Item)
Lead
Task
questions.explain: The lesson explains Opportunity Product (Line Item) attaches specific products, quantities, and prices to one Opportunity -- this is what makes an equipment package concrete.

questions.q: Why does this lesson repeat that Cascade Foodservice Equipment Co. is fictional?
options: To make clear it's an illustrative scenario for practice, not a real business or case study, consistent with how this catalog handles invented capstone scenarios
Because the course will later reveal it is based on a real company
Because fictional companies are required by Salesforce's terms of service
Because the name was legally trademarked by another organization
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states, more than once, that Cascade is fictional and illustrative, invented purely to give this capstone one consistent, concrete scenario to build around.

questions.q: Why does Priya Nair's Key Accounts role report directly to Monica Reyes instead of through Derek Oyelaran?
options: Because Salesforce role hierarchies cannot have more than two levels
Because Oyelaran has no profile that allows managing other roles
Because Nair does not use the Sales Manager profile
Because Key Accounts deals are large and sensitive, and Cascade doesn't want the New Business manager seeing them by default
questions.explain: The lesson states this placement is deliberate: Key Accounts deals are large and sensitive, so they stay out of Oyelaran's default role-hierarchy visibility by placing Nair directly under Reyes.

questions.q: What does the Path component at the top of the Opportunity layout visually represent?
options: The list of products attached to the Opportunity
A visual tracker showing progress through Cascade's stages, from Qualifying to Closed Won
The Account's billing address history
A chart of the sales team's monthly quota attainment
questions.explain: The lesson describes the Path as a visual Lightning component showing progress through Opportunity Stage -- from Qualifying through Closed Won -- placed at the top of the layout.

questions.q: Why is `Opportunity__c` on Installation Project created as a Lookup relationship rather than Master-Detail?
options: Lookup relationships are the only type available on custom objects
Master-Detail would force Installation Project's sharing to follow Opportunity exactly, which conflicts with the separate Lesson 4 sharing rule for the Service & Installation team
Master-Detail relationships cannot reference the Opportunity object
Lookup fields automatically roll up Annual Value to the parent
questions.explain: The lesson explains this is the same Lesson 3/4 decision carried into the field wizard: Lookup avoids coupling Installation Project's sharing tightly to Opportunity's, which would conflict with the dedicated Service & Installation sharing rule.

questions.q: Per this lesson's field-level security guidance, which profiles get Edit access on the new Account and Contact fields, and which get Read Only?
options: Sales Rep and Sales Manager get Edit; Service and Customer Success profiles get Read Only
Only System Administrator gets any access at all
Service and Customer Success get Edit; Sales profiles get Read Only
All profiles get Edit access equally
questions.explain: The lesson specifies Sales Rep and Sales Manager get Edit access since this is sales-owned data, while Service and Customer Success profiles get Read Only.

questions.q: In the walked-through example, what does Tom Baptiste do right after the site visit, and what stage does the Opportunity move to?
options: He sets Stage to Closed Won immediately after the visit
He adds products (the range and the hood) and moves the Opportunity to Needs Analysis
He marks the deal Closed Lost due to no budget
He reassigns the Opportunity to Priya Nair
questions.explain: The walkthrough describes Tom adding the range and hood products after the site visit and then moving the Opportunity to the Needs Analysis stage.

questions.q: What are Cascade's four Lead Source picklist values?
options: Cold Call, Email Blast, Billboard, Radio Ad
Trade Show, Website Inquiry, Referral, Partner/Dealer
Inbound, Outbound, Marketing Qualified, Sales Qualified
LinkedIn, Google Ads, Direct Mail, Walk-In
questions.explain: The lesson sets the Lead Source picklist to exactly these four values, matching the lead channels introduced in Lesson 2: Trade Show, Website Inquiry, Referral, and Partner/Dealer.

questions.q: Why is the service-visit Screen Flow launched as a Quick Action on the Installation Project layout instead of asking installers to use the standard Edit screen?
options: The standard Edit screen doesn't exist on custom objects
Quick Actions are required for all Screen Flows
It gives installers a fast, focused way to log a visit from the field without exposing the full record edit layout or fields outside their job
It's the only way to update a picklist field in Salesforce
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a usability and scope choice -- a guided, two-screen flow for a specific field task, instead of the full edit layout.

questions.q: What does the Annual_Value_Positive rule on Service Contract enforce?
options: Annual Value must be greater than zero
Annual Value must match the Opportunity Amount exactly
Annual Value must be a whole number
Annual Value can only be set by Angela Wu
questions.explain: The error condition is Annual_Value__c <= 0, which blocks a zero or negative value before it ever reaches a renewal report.

questions.q: Why is Monica Reyes assigned as a specified-user approver instead of using a role-hierarchy-based approver like "submitter's manager"?
options: Specified-user approvers are required for every Salesforce approval process
Role-hierarchy-based approval isn't supported on the Opportunity object
The discount threshold applies the same way regardless of which branch of the hierarchy the Opportunity owner sits in, including Priya Nair, who doesn't report through Derek Oyelaran
Monica Reyes doesn't have a role in the hierarchy
questions.explain: Because Priya Nair reports directly to Monica while Tom Baptiste reports through Derek Oyelaran, a role-based approver wouldn't route both consistently to Monica -- naming her directly does.

questions.q: Which role sits at the very top of Cascade's role hierarchy, built in this lesson?
options: VP of Sales (Monica Reyes)
Sales Manager, New Business (Derek Oyelaran)
Senior AE, Key Accounts (Priya Nair)
System Administrator
questions.explain: Monica Reyes's VP of Sales role is the root of the seven-role hierarchy; every other role sits beneath it.

questions.q: Why does this lesson use Data Loader rather than the Import Wizard for Installation Projects and Service Contracts?
options: The Import Wizard cannot create records at all
Data Loader supports custom objects and multiple related lookups per row, and handles bulk CSV loads the Wizard isn't built for
Installation Projects don't support any lookup fields
Data Loader is required for every object with a picklist field
questions.explain: Data Loader is chosen for its bulk insert/upsert capability and support for custom objects with multiple lookup relationships per row.

questions.q: Which three things does Section 8 (Known Limitations) explicitly say this build does NOT include?
options: Reports, dashboards, and sample data
Role hierarchy, profiles, and sharing rules
Lightning Web Components, integration with an outside ERP/accounting system, and Apex
Validation rules, Flows, and an approval process
questions.explain: The lesson lists these three specifically, framing the build as intentionally, fully declarative -- consistent with Lesson 1's 'declarative build' definition.

questions.q: In the Section 1 security tests, what should happen when Derek Oyelaran logs in and views Opportunities?
options: He sees every Opportunity in the org
He sees Tom Baptiste's and Jordan Kessler's records, but not Priya Nair's
He sees nothing, since Sales Managers have no Opportunity access
He sees only his own records, with no rollup from his team
questions.explain: Role hierarchy rolls access up to Oyelaran for his direct reports (Baptiste and Kessler) but not for Nair, whose role reports directly to Monica Reyes instead.

questions.q: Which chapter closed out Requirements 4 through 7 of the Lesson 1 Definition of Done (security model, Flows, validation rules, approval process)?
options: Chapter 1 -- Design
Chapter 2 -- Build: Data and Objects
Chapter 3 -- Build: Automation and Security
Chapter 4 -- Analytics and Delivery
questions.explain: Chapter 3 (Lessons 11-14) implemented the security model, both Flows, all four validation rules, and the approval process.

questions.q: Why does the Cascade Executive Dashboard run as Monica Reyes instead of "run as logged-in user"?
options: Dashboards can only run as the System Administrator
Running as Monica Reyes guarantees the dashboard always shows the full picture her role hierarchy position entitles her to see, regardless of who's viewing it
It's required whenever a dashboard includes more than two components
Monica Reyes is the only user with a Sales Manager profile
questions.explain: Because Private OWD plus the Lesson 11 role hierarchy means Monica sees every record beneath her, a fixed running user guarantees consistent, complete results.
